episodes.problem: Swift bars rect-snapped in swift_orange but traced as curves in swift_orange_solid
episodes.first_read: The isoperimetric complexity gate was rejecting long thin bars.
episodes.evidence: Per-column histogram of the solid bar: 3 stray antialiasing pixels out of 268,100. minAreaRect bounded them and stretched the bar 89 to 91 px tall across 2980 px; coverage 0.9993 to 0.9776, under the gate. On a 300 px bar the same crumbs also tilted it 0.28 degrees.
episodes.cause: minAreaRect is a bounding estimator, so a handful of outlier pixels sets both the size and the angle of the whole rectangle.
episodes.fix: Consensus fit: extents from a ladder of boundary trims, orientation from second moments, coverage picks the winner with the bounding fit still in the running.
episodes.verified: All 926 corpus elements: 5 newly named, 0 worse. swift_orange_solid ideality 0.8502 to 0.8791.
episodes.method: When a fit passes on one variant and fails on its near-twin, diff the inputs pixel by pixel before touching any threshold — the cause is usually a few pixels that a bounding or least-squares estimator lets decide. Use a consensus estimator and let a measured quantity choose among candidates.

episodes.problem: best_fit ranked a rectangle covering 0.80 above a polygon covering 0.97 on the same element
episodes.first_read: The consensus rect change had caused a regression on propak.
episodes.evidence: Scanning all candidates showed 14 elements where the degrees-of-freedom preference cost up to 17 points of coverage, predating the change.
episodes.cause: 'Prefer the constrained shape when both fit' was implemented as 'when both clear the floor', and the floor is a minimum that relaxes to 0.80 on small elements.
episodes.fix: A freer shape outranks a tighter one only if it removes most of the tighter one's leftover error (as a fraction), and only while material error remains.
episodes.verified: Element scan: 5 renamed, every one to a better fit; propak regression gone.
episodes.method: Clearing a floor is not proof of fitting. Compare candidates by how much of the remaining error a freer model removes, measured as a fraction so it means the same at every size — and stop asking once the remaining error is immaterial, or the test turns hair-trigger.

episodes.problem: Reconstruction took about 5 minutes per logo
episodes.first_read: Glyphs are compared at 64x64, so rendering them at 256 px is obvious waste — render smaller.
episodes.evidence: At 128 px the normalized bitmap agreed with the 256 px one at only 0.9603 mean and 0.8510 at the 1st percentile, against a 0.86 match threshold and a winning score of 0.9545. It would have changed which font was chosen, for a 2.1x gain. Profiling cold and warm separately showed rendering, not comparison, was 98% of the time — and each logo is a fresh process.
episodes.cause: Every process re-rendered 1,562 fonts across 66 characters.
episodes.fix: Render once at full quality into a memory-mapped glyph store built on first use; hoist the corpus scan out of the two-candidate loop; exact branch-and-bound in match_run.
episodes.verified: Cold start 265.3 s to 6.9 s; identical matches to the last digit (ScienceGothic-400, SUPPLY, 0.954527).
episodes.method: An optimisation that should change nothing must be shown to change nothing — measure its effect at the decision threshold before shipping it. Profile cold and warm paths separately; a per-process tool pays the cold cost every time.

episodes.problem: Reported a 0.0035 regression in the default path that did not exist
episodes.first_read: The shape-fitting change had regressed Swift vectorize anchors 0.9269 to 0.9234.
episodes.evidence: The re-run used --min-height 3000 and two engines; every historical run used 1200 and three. Re-run at matching settings reproduced 0.9269 / 0.9356 exactly.
episodes.cause: Nothing recorded the configuration beside the score, so incomparable runs looked comparable.
episodes.fix: min_height and engines are now recorded on every row, in the summary and in the durable run snapshots.
episodes.verified: Guardrail reproduced the baseline to four decimals.
episodes.method: Never compare two runs until their configuration matches, and record configuration beside every score so the check is possible. A surprising regression is a configuration difference until proven otherwise.

episodes.problem: The reconstruction gate could not tell which candidate was better within a pair
episodes.first_read: Agreement with the source is the strongest signal (r=+0.57), so rank on it.
episodes.evidence: Built every candidate on all 18 pairs and scored against the clean masters. Agreement ranked candidates within a pair no better than chance; trialta's reconstruction agreed at 0.180 vs the trace's 0.914 and scored better. A Lanczos fallback agrees almost perfectly because it IS the degraded source enlarged.
episodes.cause: Agreement with the raster measures which pair is easy, and rewards changing nothing.
episodes.fix: Rule derived from the study: when the trace produced no vector, ship the reconstruction unless it collapsed; tie-break reconstruction variants by build quality.
episodes.verified: Corpus composite 0.7433 to 0.7567, v2 0.7455 to 0.7584, 0 regressions; the re-run matched the study to four decimals.
episodes.method: A signal strong across cases can be useless within one. Validate a ranking signal inside the unit you are choosing within, and derive decision rules from a ground-truth study rather than argument. Fidelity to a degraded input rewards doing nothing.

episodes.problem: The three largest reported wins had deleted GCM's red monogram
episodes.first_read: composite ranked them the best candidates in the corpus (e.g. 0.8373 to 0.8619).
episodes.evidence: Looking at the comparison sheet: the red C/G was gone. Red share of ink 0.108 in the master, 0.000 in the output.
episodes.cause: Layers were seeded from exact 5-bit colour bins, so a JPEG-mottled red spread over dozens of sub-threshold bins never got a layer; and the white page counted as the largest 'ink' colour.
episodes.fix: Pool bins into colours before seeding; remove the page (a neutral that owns the border); resolve antialiasing ramps and halos by hue family.
episodes.verified: Red retained in 12/12 degraded variants, halos in 0/12; clean masters reduce to their true brand palettes.
episodes.method: Never report an improvement without looking at the output. A blended score can rank a logo with a deleted element as the best result — the missing element is only part of one term.

episodes.problem: Removing JPEG halos deleted PROPAK's red rule
episodes.first_read: A thin colour attached to another colour is a halo.
episodes.evidence: Checking red explicitly after the change: the rule has interior 0.000 at that size and sits beside its own pink fringe, so a pairwise test could read either as the halo of the other. It survived one run by 0.08 margin.
episodes.cause: The rule was a single pairwise property; paint and rust can share it.
episodes.fix: One colour per hue family: interior means paint; thin and sharing a painted colour's hue means fringe; an all-thin family keeps its strongest member.
episodes.verified: Red kept everywhere, halos gone everywhere.
episodes.method: When removing a class of artefact, explicitly re-check every element you meant to keep. A rule that removes rust will remove paint that resembles rust in the one respect the rule tests. Passing by a small margin is luck, not a fix.

episodes.first_read: The reviewer was right and the outputs had lost colours.
episodes.evidence: Pixel counts showed the outputs kept them: Swift's black shadow read as (2,0,0), HSV saturation 1.0, and was taken for red; GCM's navy text crushed to (0,1,12) read as black, so bringing it back blue was called a deletion.
episodes.cause: HSV saturation explodes near black; dark colours carry their hue as a faint tint that a chroma threshold discards.
episodes.fix: Absolute chroma everywhere, a dark-tint rule, and review against both the raw and prepared sketches.
episodes.verified: Against clean masters over every candidate: 14 real deletions caught, 0 false alarms, 0 missed.
episodes.method: Test a reviewer for false alarms against ground truth before trusting it — a reviewer that cries wolf gets ignored. Use absolute chroma, never HSV saturation, anywhere near black.

episodes.problem: Meedo-Me's advice showed a 0% hit rate
episodes.evidence: All 28 proposals had been judged without anyone acting on them; nobody read the file all session. Its most repeated proposal was a correct diagnosis of the next problem.
episodes.cause: Proposals were scored by whether their case happened to move, whether or not they were taken; and repeats were filed as new proposals.
episodes.fix: Decide before judging (accept with a baseline run, reject with a reason); escalate repeats; learn which engines not to propose on from rejection patterns; a standup at the start of every work cycle, written into CLAUDE.md.
episodes.verified: 28 proposals became 11; first standup decided 10; Meedo-Me learned to stop proposing on baseline and esrgan.
episodes.method: Advice is only tested once someone acts on it — measure advice from acceptance, not from filing. Put the advisor in the path of the work, or it becomes a diary.

episodes.problem: Identify the typeface of the orange SWIFT letters
episodes.first_read: Run the glyph matcher against the corpus.
episodes.evidence: Best match GravitasOne at 0.83, visibly a different face. The corpus is essentially Google Fonts. Web search found nothing for the logo.
episodes.cause: Commercial display type and custom lettering are outside a free-font corpus.
episodes.fix: Named the genre with confidence (ultra-bold italic wedge-serif display type; the slashes are a logo treatment), declined to invent a name, and gave a clean isolated extraction for WhatTheFont / Matcherator.
episodes.method: A weak top match in a limited corpus means 'not in the corpus', not 'closest relative'. Say so plainly and hand over the clean input a proper identifier needs.

episodes.problem: A check suggested the SUPPLY font substitution was wrong
episodes.evidence: The check had included the two orange bars as 'letters', shifting every comparison by two. Corrected: 0.9545 mean, 0.924-0.985 per letter.
episodes.cause: A bug in my own verification script.
episodes.fix: Fixed the check; the substitution was sound.
episodes.method: When a check contradicts a strong earlier result, suspect the check first — print exactly what it is comparing before acting on its verdict.

episodes.problem: Blur washed brand colours toward the page (TRIALTA green to mint, Arc and PROPAK red to pink)
episodes.first_read: Sample each element's densest ink — the pixels furthest from the page.
episodes.evidence: Degraded-only measurement: 0 worse. But the clean PROPAK master's red (199,48,47) became (50,15,14): its densest pixels were edges mixed with the dark blue letters. A chroma-based variant instead picked halos that prepare_for_engine had oversaturated, turning GCM navy cyan. Unconstrained sampling also drifted PROPAK's red toward blue-grey from neighbouring bleed.
episodes.cause: Two purity estimators each fooled by a different contaminant; the real question is whether the element is washed at all.
episodes.fix: Restore only when the element's average sits near the page (<=340 L1; washed 123-288, solid fills >=405) AND differs from its densest same-hue ink by >=110; sample only same-hue pixels; never touch neutrals.
episodes.verified: 6 layers restored, 0 worse, all 6 clean masters unchanged; mean error to intended colour 55.5 to 39.8; visually green and red return. PROPAK's thin rule only reaches 224 off — no pixel in the sketch is pure, and going further would invent.
episodes.method: Gate a restoration on the condition it restores, and verify clean inputs stay unchanged — not only that damaged ones improve. When a 'purity' estimate is fooled, ask which contaminant fooled it; two different contaminants mean the estimator is the wrong question.

episodes.problem: Meedo-Me's memory was reachable only from Python in this repo; the Jan-based app, Claude Code and agents each needed it
episodes.first_read: Build a context-stitching engine inside the Jan fork
episodes.evidence: Jan already speaks MCP natively, as do Claude Code and most agents; an engine inside Jan would tie the memory to one client
episodes.cause: Memory and its faces were coupled by design choice, not necessity
episodes.fix: A zero-dependency stdio MCP server over the ledger, reviewer and episodes; read-only mode drops every writer; reviewer paths confined to the repo and MEEDO_ALLOWED_DIRS
episodes.verified: Official MCP SDK 2.2.0 client drove both modes end to end; 10 unit tests including symlink escape, foreign cwd, and stdout purity while a tool prints
episodes.method: Serve shared memory over a protocol every face already speaks instead of building it into one face. Verify a protocol implementation with the official client, not a reading of the spec. On stdio, route prints to stderr — one stray line corrupts the session.

episodes.problem: small same-colour elements dropped (GCM Modification i-dots); reviewer colour-only missed them
episodes.first_read: brand_colour share barely moved while separate blobs vanished
episodes.evidence: synthetic navy word+dots: colour check passed, element_count blocked after drop of 2+ components below 70% keep
episodes.cause: reviewer measured ink share by hue family, not connected components
episodes.method: count connected ink components (area>=8) on sketch vs output; block when drop>=2 and keep<70%

episodes.evidence: sketch has 32 ink elements, output has 8 (24 dropped) — small same-colour pieces are missing

episodes.problem: Trialta letterforms collapse to blobs; font match named nothing on clean TRIALTA
episodes.first_read: glyph matching broken or fonts missing
episodes.evidence: mixed-colour run gray TRI+green ALTA scored 0.807 < MIN_RUN_SCORE 0.86; colour-segregated runs scored 0.87–0.95 Oswald; icon fragments diluted gray TRI until contiguous subsequences recovered T,R,I
episodes.cause: group_runs ignored fill colour, so two designed words were scored as one typesetting pass; baseline-sharing icon scrap diluted TRI
episodes.method: Segregate glyph runs by colour family; filter hairlines; on failed runs try contiguous subsequences. Keep element_count on compact satellites only and skip when sketch has >4 (JPEG crumbs).
